blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Average is calculated by dividing the sum of all observations by the total number of observations.
The total sum of observations can be determined by multiplying the given average by the total count (Sum = Average × Count).
Adding or removing a value changes the overall average proportionally based on the difference from the initial mean.
If the current average age of a group of N individuals is A, their average age after Y years will be A + Y.
Weighted average is used when combined groups have different sizes or relative importances.
Average of a group of numbers is a single value that represents the central value of the group.

Formula:

Average = (Sum of observations) / (Number of observations)

blocks.content: 3. FINDING SUM WHEN AVERAGE IS GIVEN

items:
Formula:

Sum = Average × Number of observations

Example:

Average age of 10 students is 18 years.

Total age = 18 × 10 = 180 years

blocks.content: 4. AVERAGE WHEN A VALUE IS ADDED OR REMOVED

Example 1:

Average of 5 numbers is 20. A new number 30 is added.

Old sum = 20 × 5 = 100

New sum = 100 + 30 = 130

New number of observations = 6

New average = 130 / 6 ≈ 21.67



Example 2:

Average of 10 numbers is 25. One number 35 is removed.

Old sum = 25 × 10 = 250

New sum = 250 − 35 = 215

New number of observations = 9

New average = 215 / 9 ≈ 23.89
